answer: A Weekly community check-in streak over six months verified by attendance records makes identity a record of showing up: every week the applicant signs in, the attendance records go on the public record, and one missed week resets the streak to zero, so the network trusts the account that was there every week, not the one that appeared yesterday. The system trusts a thread only after it survives the full season of checks. From the shale to the mirror, the same rule holds: no presence, no trust, no exception.
